sources.name: OLALLA Water System
sources.details: MARCH 11, 2025 - WQA remains in effect along with chlorination of the system. JANUARY 20, 2026 - WQA remains in effect along with chlorination of the system. NOVEMBER 6, 2025 WQA in effect. Based on recent bacteriological results, the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen (RDOS), in consultation with Interior Health, have downgraded the Boil Water Notice (BWN) that has been in effect since April 24, 2025. Total coliforms and background bacteria have been periodically reported since August 2024; the BWN was the result of an increase in the frequency and quantity being reported. The source of the contamination has yet to be determined in spite the substantial testing completed by the RDOS. As a result, the System will remain chlorinated for the foreseeable future. Currently, there is no treatment system in place for the groundwater (a single deep well), supplying the Water System. Typically, the System is monitored for potential contamination and undergoes periodic flushes and temporary chlorination as needed. This System serves approximately 250 connections. -- AUGUST 11, 2025 BWN remains in effect. This System remains under a Boil Water Notice as Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen (RDOS) has yet to determine the source of contamination, despite their continued efforts. Most recent efforts involved: • The Reservoir was isolated, and the System was ran dynamically for the last few weeks. • The Reservoir was also emptied and disinfected while offline. • Further work to improve the water quality is anticipated to take place in the fall. • Additional measures will be implemented in the coming months to prevent backflow conditions within the System, and the reservoir is expected to be lined for further source protection. -- JUNE 27, 2025 BWN remains in effect and Temporary Chlorination has been reinstated. In continued efforts to determine the source of the contamination RDOS is now planning to change the configuration of the system and informs residents that the chlorination will be turned on and off for different periods of time. -- JUNE 9, 2025 BWN remains in effect and Temporary Chlorination will be suspended to facilitate further bacteriological testing as part of on-going efforts to pinpoint the source of the contamination. Total coliforms and background bacteria have been periodically reported in water system samples since August 2024. The most recent BWN (issued April 24) is the result of an increase in the frequency and quantity being reported. In the report dated May 23, Total Coliform bacteria are present throughout the Distribution System, including the Storage Reservoir and No Total Coliform bacteria were reported from the source well. Based on the level of bacteria reported, the RDOS decided to reinstate the temporary chlorination. RDOS on-going efforts to determine the source of the contamination entering the system include: • Enhanced bacteriological sampling, • Extensive flushing of the distribution system, • Temporary chlorination (October 11, 2024 to February 18, 2025), • WQA (March 13 to 24), • BWN ISSUED APRIL 24, 2025, • Temporary chlorination (April 30 to May 9), • May 2, 2025, the RDOS hired a contractor with a Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) to inspect the inside of the storage Reservoir, and no apparent sources of contamination were noted from this inspection. • Temporary chlorination (May 23, 2025 to June 9, 2025), RDOS is now planning to isolate the storage Reservoir from the distribution system to further determine if the source of contamination is associated with the Reservoir. This will require some additional programming of the pump control system in advance to allow the system to modulate the speed of the Well Pump to continually maintain a set pressure in the distribution system while the Reservoir is isolated. Once this programming is complete, chlorination will again be removed from the system (scheduled for June 9) to allow for bacteriological testing. The Olalla System consists of a single deep source groundwater well, an elevated storage reservoir and distribution system. The water supply is typically not treated; the system is monitored for potential contamination and undergoes periodic flushes and temporary chlorination as needed. This System has approx. 200 service connections.

NOVEMBER 6, 2025 WQA in effect. Based on recent bacteriological results, the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen (RDOS), in consultation with Interior Health, have downgraded the Boil Water Notice (BWN) that has been in effect since April 24, 2025. Total coliforms and background bacteria have been periodically reported since August 2024; the BWN was the result of an increase in the frequency and quantity being reported. The source of the contamination has yet to be determined in spite the substantial testing completed by the RDOS. As a result, the System will remain chlorinated for the foreseeable future. Currently, there is no treatment system in place for the groundwater (a single deep well), supplying the Water System. Typically, the System is monitored for potential contamination and undergoes periodic flushes and temporary chlorination as needed. This System serves approximately 250 connections. -- AUGUST 11, 2025 BWN remains in effect. This System remains under a Boil Water Notice as Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen (RDOS) has yet to determine the source of contamination, despite their continued efforts. Most recent efforts involved: • The Reservoir was isolated, and the System was ran dynamically for the last few weeks. • The Reservoir was also emptied and disinfected while offline. • Further work to improve the water quality is anticipated to take place in the fall. • Additional measures will be implemented in the coming months to prevent backflow conditions within the System, and the reservoir is expected to be lined for further source protection. -- JUNE 27, 2025 BWN remains in effect and Temporary Chlorination has been reinstated. In continued efforts to determine the source of the contamination RDOS is now planning to change the configuration of the system and informs residents that the chlorination will be turned on and off for different periods of time. -- JUNE 9, 2025 BWN remains in effect and Temporary Chlorination will be suspended to facilitate further bacteriological testing as part of on-going efforts to pinpoint the source of the contamination. Total coliforms and background bacteria have been periodically reported in water system samples since August 2024. The most recent BWN (issued April 24) is the result of an increase in the frequency and quantity being reported. In the report dated May 23, Total Coliform bacteria are present throughout the Distribution System, including the Storage Reservoir and No Total Coliform bacteria were reported from the source well. Based on the level of bacteria reported, the RDOS decided to reinstate the temporary chlorination. RDOS on-going efforts to determine the source of the contamination entering the system include: • Enhanced bacteriological sampling, • Extensive flushing of the distribution system, • Temporary chlorination (October 11, 2024 to February 18, 2025), • WQA (March 13 to 24), • BWN ISSUED APRIL 24, 2025, • Temporary chlorination (April 30 to May 9), • May 2, 2025, the RDOS hired a contractor with a Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) to inspect the inside of the storage Reservoir, and no apparent sources of contamination were noted from this inspection. • Temporary chlorination (May 23, 2025 to June 9, 2025), RDOS is now planning to isolate the storage Reservoir from the distribution system to further determine if the source of contamination is associated with the Reservoir. This will require some additional programming of the pump control system in advance to allow the system to modulate the speed of the Well Pump to continually maintain a set pressure in the distribution system while the Reservoir is isolated. Once this programming is complete, chlorination will again be removed from the system (scheduled for June 9) to allow for bacteriological testing. sources.name: Dease Lake Air Tanker Base Water System (building #72116)
sources.underlying_problems: A sample of the treated water was taken on January 27, 2026 for general chemical analysis which led to a determination that the guideline limit for arsenic (0.01 mg/L) had been exceeded – result was 0.0650 mg/L. The source for this water system is a deep well (WTN 49208) which draws from an aquifer that has naturally high arsenic. A treatment system has been installed and includes a component for lowering arsenic to below to guideline limit. It appears this treatment system component requires maintenance (i.e., media replacement). Other treatment system components also appear to require maintenance as the system for lowering hardness appears to be non-functinal, and the system for lowering manganese appears to be only partially effective. This water system is mostly used seasonally from May to October and only one of two connected buildings are in use at this time. As a precaution for maintenance and custodial staff who may infrequently use the connected building, the operator has posted Do Not Consume notices at points where drinking water can be obtained. This notice will remain in effect until additional testing can be done, the treatment system is repaired and/or maintained to ensure it’s performing as designed, performance of the treatment system is verified through additional testing, a trained operator is in place, and written operations & maintenance procedures are available for the operator.
sources.steps_taken_to_remedy: Per the plan detailed under corrective actions.
sources.corrective_actions_remaining: 1) Submit a follow-up sample of treated water for general chemical analysis to verify the treatment system is non-funtional. 2) Based on results of the follow-up sample, take whatever corrective actions are required to repair and/or maintain treatment system components. 3) After repairs and/or maintenance is complete, submit a sample to determine if the treatment system is performing as designed. 4) Provide an operator who is capable of operating & maintaining the treatment system and other components of the water system. 5) Provide a written set of procedures which details how each treatment system and water system component is to be operated & maintained.

sources.underlying_problems: On March 3, 2026, the operator collected a chemical sample from the storage tank. The results showed a turbidity level of 20 NTU. Since that time, the operator has repaired the isolation valve on the carbon bed. Follow-up turbidity sampling of the water after UV treatment—prior to entering the storage tank—indicated a turbidity level of 2.3 NTU. This does not meet the surface water objective treatments and could impact the effectiveness of chlorination and UV treatment.
sources.steps_taken_to_remedy: Operator posted Boil Water Notice signage at all water faucets to ensure users were immediately informed of the advisory. Operator notified all employees and water users of the advisory. Operator has provided potable water for consumption.

sources.name: Skidegate Ferry Terminal Water System
sources.underlying_problems: Chlorine residual disinfection is below the required 0.2 mg/L most days during operation. Precautionary boil water notice in place until a suitable solution to the low residual is found.
sources.steps_taken_to_remedy: - Terminal maintenance personelle are working with a consultant to determine if an automatic chlorine pump can be added to the system to increase the chlorine residual. - Staff use bottled water within the facility.
sources.corrective_actions_remaining: - Operator to notify water users of system update. - Determine an appropriate chlorine pump to add residual to the system. - Apply for a construction permit from the Public Health Engineer - Once permit received install the chlorine pump. - Flush the system and ensure the chlorine residual is above the required 0.2 mg/L at the end of the line. - Two bacteriological samples, taken 24 hours apart, showing absence of total coliforms and E.coli must be reported.

sources.underlying_problems: - Recent bacteriological sampling of the water system detected 10 Total Coliforms and 3 E. coli. - Operator suspects the adverse sample results due to a sampling error. - Operator mentioned it was a different person who collected the sample this time and the sampler did not disinfect the faucet before collecting the sample. - This water system supplies a cut and wrap facility.
sources.steps_taken_to_remedy: - EHO has contacted and explained the situation to the operator and issued a Boil Water Notice on the water system. - Operator will take responsibility to ensure all users are informed about the Boil Water Notice. - Operator to ensure boil water notice signs are posted at all water taps within the food premises. - The Operator is to advise the water users to boil all drinking water to a rolling boil for a minimum of one (1) minute prior to consumption. - EHO has provided information on how to operate food services during a BWN. - Sampling procedures were reviewed with the operator.
sources.corrective_actions_remaining: - Collect bacteriological samples using proper sampling technique, including faucet disinfection. - Submit two bacteriological water samples showing the absence of total coliforms and E.coli. Each sample must be taken at least 24 hours apart. - Contact the Environmental Health Officer to review the results and rescind the boil water notice if applicable.

raw.steps_taken_to_remedy: - EHO has contacted and explained the situation to the operator and issued a Boil Water Notice on the water system. - Operator will take responsibility to ensure all users are informed about the Boil Water Notice. - Operator to ensure boil water notice signs are posted at all water taps within the food premises. - The Operator is to advise the water users to boil all drinking water to a rolling boil for a minimum of one (1) minute prior to consumption. - EHO has provided information on how to operate food services during a BWN. - Sampling procedures were reviewed with the operator.
raw.corrective_actions_remaining: - Collect bacteriological samples using proper sampling technique, including faucet disinfection. - Submit two bacteriological water samples showing the absence of total coliforms and E.coli. Each sample must be taken at least 24 hours apart. - Contact the Environmental Health Officer to review the results and rescind the boil water notice if applicable.

sources.name: Kitimat Community Water System
sources.facility_location: East of Kitimat River near Highway Bridge, Kitimat
sources.underlying_problems: The Kitimat water system draws water from the Kitimat River via two infiltration galleries which provide partial filtration for turbidity; however, as the water level in the river rises the effectiveness of the filtration goes down. Historically, at a water level of 1.8 m the turbidity of water post infiltration goes over 1 NTU which reduces the effectiveness of chlorine disinfection and makes it difficult to maintain a minimum residual of 0.2 ppm free chlorine throughout the distribution system. Snow melt has lead to an increased water level in the river and higher turbidity post infiltration (1.17 NTU). While the water supplier stored clean water when the river level was < 1.8 m, reservoir levels were at the point where dirty water needed to be pumped into the system on the night of May 6 2026 to ensure a sufficient volume is available for fire protection. The turbidity in the system is still >1 NTU as of the morning of May 7 2026. However, the water level has dropped since then and the advisory is expected to remain in place until tomorrow afternoon dependent on turbidity results. The underlying problem for this water system is that there is inadequate treatment of water from the surface water source.
sources.steps_taken_to_remedy: Pump only as much high turbidity water as is necessary into the system and verify a minimum of 0.2 ppm free chlorine can be maintained. If free chlorine cannot be maintained above 0.2 ppm throughout the distribution system or if the water post infiltration goes over 5 NTU, this WQA will likely be upgraded to a Boil Water Notice.
sources.corrective_actions_remaining: Flush dirty water from the system and maintain a minimum 0.2 ppm free chlorine residual and establish a turbidity level of < 1 NTU throughout the distribution system.

sources.name: RUSSETT BLUFF
sources.details: The Cariboo Regional District (CRD) has issued a Boil Water Notice and Water Quality Advisory in the RUSSETT BLUFF area. The CRD says the Notice has been issued as the system is transitioned to the Lower Well, as the Upper Well aquifer can no longer meet the seasonal demand. THE WQA was issued because of high concentrations of manganese in the Lower Well that exceed the maximum allowed by Health Canada. Since boiling water will increase the manganese concentration. infants and young children absorb more manganese and cannot regulate and eliminate it as readily as adult
